A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EEG-FM-Bench. Their text, equations, tables, rendered figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments for five EEG foundation models across 14 datasets, including quantitative results and representation visualizations.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmarking results for seven EEG models and two general time-series models, plus adaptation, initialization, classifier, and optimization-dynamics experiments.

M1.justification: The benchmark gains LoRA adaptation, attention-pooling decoding, and a diagnostic procedure collecting and projecting gradients and intermediate representations (Sections 3.2–3.3). These substantially extend its procedures. The large-MLP variant already appeared in v1 Appendix C.4 and is expanded rather than newly introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14 datasets covering the same 10 EEG paradigms and classification tasks. Dataset descriptions and sample counts match between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 1. New model and analysis configurations do not introduce additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds CSBrain and REVE to the five-model EEG comparisons and evaluates Mantis and Moment as general time-series comparators (Tables 2–6 and 9). Classifier-head comparisons also expand from CBraMod alone in v1 Appendix C.4 to LaBraM, CBraMod, CSBrain, and REVE in v2 Tables 7–8.

E3.justification: Reported filtering changes from 0.1–128 Hz to 0.1–100 Hz, universal 256 Hz resampling becomes model-specific, and training/warm-up budgets change from 50/5 to 30/3 epochs. v2 adds grid search, freezing warm-up, and scratch/LoRA/probing protocols; frozen-backbone evaluation changes from single-task to multi-task. SEED-VII is newly described as subject-dependent while its subject-split bullet remains unchanged, leaving that setting unresolved. These descriptions do not establish which retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic scratch-versus-pretrained controls, broader adaptation and head ablations, scaling analysis, cross-task and cross-objective gradient diagnostics, layer-wise CKA/RSA, and a CSBrain optimization-failure analysis. These substantially extend v1's limited head comparison and qualitative analyses. The original SEED/Workload t-SNE and saliency panel is removed.

E5.justification: Five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains for benchmark performance. v2 separately specifies ten-seed aggregation for diagnostic probing, but removes v1 Appendix E's EEGPT–CBraMod paired t-test, confidence interval, and effect size. This does not establish an increase in runs for retained benchmark results.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for new comparators, LoRA, scratch training, classifier heads, and diagnostic analyses, while revising some retained entries. For example, CBraMod's single-task SEED balanced accuracy changes from 70.83 ± 0.28 to 62.59 ± 2.40 in Table 2. Given the revised protocol descriptions, this is a changed reported result, not an established same-setting deterioration.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.3 introduces mathematical definitions for diagnostic quantities, including gradient-subspace affinity, conflict indicators, normalized gradient-energy shares, and representation similarity. The existing classification-metric definitions are retained. Neither version develops substantive theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 makes optimization diagnostics and pre-training efficiency central contributions, adding explicit claims that reconstruction/classification gradient conflicts limit transfer and that compact EEG-specific architectures outperform larger models despite greater pre-training scale. It also drops v1's repeated claim to be the first comprehensive EEG-FM benchmark. The generalization-gap and multi-task-benefit claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds mechanisms linking transfer to shared normalization/embedding components, pre-training benefits to backbone stabilization, and LoRA effectiveness to pretrained representation quality. It interprets CSBrain's scratch-training collapse and expands negative-transfer discussion toward conflict-aware updates and adaptive task weighting. These substantially extend v1's largely architectural and neurophysiological interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 adds probe implementation details and CSBrain/REVE adapter instructions, and updates hardware/software from A100 GPUs/CUDA 12.4 to A800 GPUs/CUDA 12.8. It drops v1's explicit 128- and 512-unit classifier sizes without supplying grid-search ranges or concrete LoRA hyperparameters. Code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v1 positions the work around the absence of a comprehensive EEG-FM benchmark. v2 acknowledges AdaBrain-Bench and Lee et al.'s EEG-FM evaluations, redefining the gap around multi-task capability, classifier configuration, efficiency, and internal dynamics. References supporting REVE, general time-series comparators, LoRA, and diagnostic techniques broaden this revised positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, pipeline description, and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. v1's model-by-model results discussion and separate Further Discussion section give way to question-focused analyses in v2 Sections 4.2–4.6. The title and appendix organization also change.

P2.justification: The pipeline diagram is redrawn; main-text numerical comparisons move into merged, transposed appendix tables. Radar charts, scaling plots, heatmaps, and training-dynamics plots reshape the main presentation. Retained appendix t-SNE/saliency figures gain CSBrain and REVE columns, while the original main qualitative panel disappears. Appendix layout also changes substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful scratch controls, broader adaptation/head comparisons, and quantitative diagnostics absent from v1. However, Tables 4 and 6 contain unexplained identical LaBraM result blocks across different tasks, Appendix B.3 contradicts itself on SEED-VII splitting, and stronger scaling claims rely on comparisons that confound architecture and scale. These unresolved reporting and evidential problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
